newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Werner sees risks if VAT lowered.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Werner sees risks if VAT lowered.

text.p: Mexico's Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Thursday cutting value added tax to 10 percent from its current 15 percent level would mean some 20 billion pesos in lost revenues.

"It would mean a drop in revenues of around 20 billion pesos and no one wants to raise public debt by 20 billion pesos because that would mean passing the bill to future generations of Mexicans," he told reporters.

Opposition parties campaigned to cut VAT ahead of July 6 mid-term elections. After they unseated the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) from its 68-year majority in the lower house of Congress, they vowed to make good on their pledges.
They have different plans on how to enact the tax cuts, however.

Interviewed during a meeting of government, business and labor leaders to assess growth and anti-inflation measures, Werner said he saw the tax issue as part of a broader fiscal reform that he insisted should not lead to a higher level of debt.
Business leaders said they also favored VAT reductions, but in a way that would not disrupt other aspects of the economy.
